style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: A matte clay 3D mechanical assembly on a weathered concrete workbench: a commitment-ladder rack of twelve machined bays, one loaded annual-charge block with a latched cover, eleven empty zero-month slots, and a brass break-even flag at the tenth bay. Bone white, graphite, and rust palette; one directional key light from the left raking across brushed steel and matte polymer, throwing a long cast shadow to the right; extreme asymmetric framing with the rack off-centre; 100mm macro focal plane, shallow depth of field, fine film grain. No text, no lettering.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos, numbers
rationale: The story is a structural, abstract pricing mechanism — an annual plan as a loan, a break-even month, and an invisible annual charge. Clay_render can state the idea as a small physical assembly of recognisable engineered parts, making the commitment ladder and zero-month slots tangible without a literal photograph.
cue: An annual plan is a loan, not a discount
subject: a matte clay mechanical commitment-ladder rack with one loaded annual-charge module and eleven empty monthly slots on a workbench
core_thesis: An annual plan is a loan, not a discount: the annual price divided by the monthly price gives the break-even month, and an annual charge is invisible to a monthly audit.
core_conflict: A monthly subscription-waste audit versus a once-a-year prepaid charge, where longer-term commitment rungs trade deeper discounts for later break-even months.

review.reason: The loaded annual-charge module set among empty monthly slots is the article's own mechanism — a prepay ladder where one periodic charge sits invisible next to the monthly rungs — rather than a foreign industry or generic filler.
